conversations.reply: So sorry you've had to deal with that, it's completely unacceptable. You deserve so much better than people who can't see past your disability.

conversations.title: Exclusive | Single women say men with roommates is the new dating dealbreaker: ‘It’s a heavy no for me’
conversations.reply: Having roommates might be a dealbreaker for some, but for disabled people, it's often the little things like accessibility that can make or break a date.

conversations.title: Attorney Karla Gilbride on challenges facing people with disabilities
conversations.reply: Karla's speaking out about the challenges she's faced is really important, and I'm glad she's using her voice to raise awareness about the issues that matter.

conversations.title: Great British Summer Savings is a brand opportunity, but accessibility will make it fly
conversations.reply: Accessibility is key to making events like the Great British Summer Savings work for everyone, and it's great to see people talking about it.

conversations.title: Las Vegas clubs to offer free admission for 21st birthday
conversations.reply: Free admission is a nice perk, but I hope these clubs are also thinking about how to make their venues accessible to everyone, regardless of ability.

conversations.title: Diecast neighbours tell of 'constant anxiety' over venue noise
conversations.reply: Noise can be a real issue for people with sensory sensitivities, and venues need to think about how they can create a more inclusive environment for everyone.

conversations.title: Aurora proclamation of Disability Pride Month seen as part of efforts to better support residents with disabilities
conversations.reply: It's fantastic to see cities like Aurora recognizing Disability Pride Month and making efforts to support their residents with disabilities, it's a great step in the right direction.

conversations.title: ‘We slept with three of the same women’: 12 people on what it’s really like dating a friend’s ex
conversations.reply: Dating can be complicated, and when you add disability to the mix, it can get even more complex. I think it's time we had a more nuanced conversation about relationships and disability.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.
